identity.title: Learning to See Before Seeing: Demystifying LLM Visual Priors from Language Pre-training

problem.claim: The paper investigates how visual priors emerge during language pre-training and how they can be deliberately cultivated for multimodal LLMs.

contributions.claim: Decomposes visual priors into separable perception and reasoning priors with distinct scaling trends and origins.
Proposes a data-centric recipe for pre-training vision-aware LLMs, verified in 1T-token-scale pre-training.
Introduces the Multi-Level Existence Bench (MLE-Bench) for future research.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a new way to deliberately cultivate visual priors from language pre-training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that latent visual reasoning is predominantly developed by reasoning-centric pre-training data such as code, mathematics, and academia, and scales progressively.
The authors report that this language-acquired reasoning prior transfers and applies universally to visual reasoning.
The authors report over 100 controlled experiments across five model scales and the full MLLM construction pipeline, consuming 500,000 GPU-hours.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-only LLMs develop rich visual priors that can support vision tasks after limited multimodal data and symbolic visual generation without images.
Systematic analysis separates visual priors into perception and reasoning components with different origins and scaling behavior.

Reasoning priors mainly arise from reasoning-centric data and scale progressively, whereas perception priors emerge diffusely and depend more on the vision encoder and visual instruction tuning; visual-world text matters but saturates quickly.
The paper turns these findings into a data-centric pre-training recipe, verifies it at 1T-token scale, and adds hypotheses plus MLE-Bench.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly separates perception and reasoning priors, then links each to different data sources, scaling trends, and adaptation sensitivities.

lessons.interpretation: A component-wise account can make a broad multimodal claim more diagnostically useful.
lessons.application: When presenting a multimodal intervention, partition the target capability into distinct priors and align each with its proposed data and scaling mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the capability cannot be meaningfully decomposed or the available evidence does not distinguish components.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs broad findings with a concrete recipe and reports verification across scales, data mixtures, and adaptation setups.

lessons.interpretation: Connecting explanatory findings to an operational recipe clarifies how analysis informs practice.
lessons.application: After identifying a data-dependent mechanism, state the resulting training recipe and specify the scale and variation dimensions used to test it.
lessons.exception: Do not present a recipe as broadly applicable when the abstract omits the recipe’s exact components or decisive evaluation conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not state a specific limitation or gap in prior work.
Exact contents of the proposed recipe, MLE-Bench, hypotheses, and 1T-token verification results are unspecified.
The meaning and measurement of “universally applicable,” “predominantly,” and rapid performance saturation are not detailed.
